Bayesian_state_estimation.credible_for_eShunt: YES — Bayesian state estimation is a different mechanism from thresholding. It maintains a probability distribution over states rather than a point estimate. Could improve noise robustness.
Bayesian_state_estimation.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM — both solve shunt failure detection, but Bayesian maintains belief distribution vs threshold on point estimate
Bayesian_state_estimation.needs_testing: Can Bayesian estimation improve on 55.8% accuracy under medium noise?

particle_filter.credible_for_eShunt: YES — particle filters handle non-linear/non-Gaussian systems, which hydraulic systems are. Could improve multi-fault discrimination.
particle_filter.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM — non-linear state estimation vs linear threshold
particle_filter.needs_testing: Can particle filter improve multi-fault classification (currently 60.3%)?

physics_informed_NN.credible_for_eShunt: PARTIAL — PINNs embed physics constraints into neural networks. Could improve identifiability under noise. But may be overcomplex for shunt diagnostics.
physics_informed_NN.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM — physics-constrained learning vs pure data-driven
physics_informed_NN.needs_testing: Does physics-informed approach improve on plain ML? (Remember: ML didn't improve on threshold.)

hybrid_model_based.credible_for_eShunt: YES — hybrid approaches combine model-based (physics) + data-driven (learning). Could address the limitation that pure ML didn't help (because it lacked physics).
hybrid_model_based.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM — combines physics model + data, vs pure threshold or pure ML
hybrid_model_based.needs_testing: Does hybrid approach outperform threshold+active (55.8%) and ML+active (55.3%)?

analysis.verdict: 4 credible alternative mechanisms identified. Bayesian and particle filter are the strongest candidates. Hybrid model-based is also promising. Physics-informed NN may be overcomplex. All need engineering comparison.

nanofiltration.credible_for_eShunt: YES — nanofiltration membranes with specific MWCO can retain therapeutic molecules while allowing CSF passage. Same coupled problem as size-selective filter.
nanofiltration.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_SAME_MECHANISM — nanofiltration IS a form of size-selective filtration. May not be architecturally different from the current candidate.
nanofiltration.risk: HIGH — may be same mechanism as current #2 candidate (size-selective filter). Need to verify architectural difference.

ion_exchange.credible_for_eShunt: PARTIAL — ion exchange retains charged molecules. Could work if therapeutic is charged. But CSF has complex ionic environment.
ion_exchange.risk: MEDIUM — requires charged therapeutic; may interfere with CSF ion balance

molecularly_imprinted.credible_for_eShunt: YES — MIPs can selectively retain specific molecules by shape/chemistry. Different from size-selective filtration.
molecularly_imprinted.risk: LOW — architecturally distinct, but needs therapeutic-specific imprinting

affinity_capture.credible_for_eShunt: YES — affinity-based capture uses antibody/receptor-ligand binding. Highly specific.
affinity_capture.same_problem_test: SAME_PROBLEM_DIFFERENT_MECHANISM — biological affinity vs physical filtration
affinity_capture.risk: MEDIUM — biological components may degrade; requires specific affinity pair

electrostatic.credible_for_eShunt: PARTIAL — electrostatic retention uses charge interactions. Requires charged therapeutic + charged membrane.
electrostatic.risk: MEDIUM — CSF ionic environment may screen charges

magnetic.credible_for_eShunt: PARTIAL — magnetic retention requires magnetic particles + external field. May not be practical for eShunt.
magnetic.risk: HIGH — requires external magnetic field; may interfere with other devices

analysis.verdict: 6 alternative mechanisms identified. MIP (molecularly imprinted polymer) and affinity capture are the strongest architecturally-distinct alternatives. Nanofiltration may be same mechanism as current candidate. Ion exchange and electrostatic are plausible but constrained. Magnetic is least practical.

analysis.assessment: Literature contains substantial work on thrombus modeling (hemodynamics + platelet + coagulation). FDA CFD benchmark data exists for blood-contacting device validation. In-vitro blood flow loop methodology exists for catheter thrombogenicity testing. The #5 thrombus model should be upgraded from composite proxy to a reduced-order model calibrated against published experimental data.
recommended_next_steps: Implement a reduced-order thrombus model: platelet activation (shear history) + residence time + coagulation cascade
Calibrate against FDA CFD benchmark nozzle geometry (available experimental data)
Validate against in-vitro blood flow loop data from published catheter studies
Then apply calibrated model to V7 FDVBZ geometry
